summary.conclusion: Exactly TWO genuinely new items this run: (1) a QA/Low operational footgun (orphaned-value-after-last-relinquish, DEDUP-NEW-001) and (2) a forward-looking spec-conformance integration assumption for the deferred stable-staker M-05 wiring (DEDUP-NEW-002). Neither is a current valid High/Medium. All other scanner signals collapse into existing acknowledged/open ledger entries, carry over un-regressed, or are dropped as false positives. No regressions: no finding previously marked 'fixed' reappeared.

findings.title: Orphaned vault value after last relinquishPrincipal: relinquishing principal until totalDeposited==0 while getTotalShares()>0 leaves residual vault value un-attributed (frozen), then capturable in full by the next single depositor on the following skimSurplus
findings.fileLine: src/AYieldStrategy.sol:638 (relinquish write-down); _skimSurplus td==0 early-return in concrete strategies
findings.rootCause: relinquishPrincipal decrements totalDeposited (and clientBalances) without disposing the backing vault shares (intended per IYieldStrategy NatSpec). When the last principal is relinquished, totalDeposited reaches 0 while getTotalShares()>0, so the residual vault value becomes un-attributable. _skimSurplus early-returns on td==0, FREEZING the residual. The instant fresh principal re-enters, a single depositor's totalBalanceOf = totalValue*principal/totalDeposited momentarily inflates to the entire position, and the next skimSurplus delivers the full residual to that recipient.
findings.impact: Mis-attribution / sequencing hazard: residual yield value can be captured in full by whoever deposits first after a full relinquish. NO value creation (value-conservation invariant holds under Tier-3 fuzzing, 128k calls across both in-scope concrete strategies); this is a redistribution/footgun, not insolvency. Non-obvious operational footgun (Law 3) for the owner/integrator sequencing relinquish-to-zero.
sources: PATTERN-003 (denominator mutation without settlement — manual-review, folds here)
findings.tier3Evidence: Value-conservation invariant holds (128k-call fuzz, both strategies). The relinquish principal-accounting skew itself (PATTERN-001 main body) is INTENDED design per IYieldStrategy NatSpec + blessed tests; only the residual-attribution / orphan-on-zero angle survives as this new QA footgun.
findings.ledgerCollision: none — no existing fingerprint covers the orphan-on-zero-totalDeposited + recapture-on-redeposit mechanism. Adjacent but distinct from QA-08 (skim-de-buffering discount-cushion footgun, different root cause) and L-01/M-02 (slippage/NAV).
findings.recommendation: Either dispose/redeem the proportional vault shares on relinquish, or block totalDeposited from reaching 0 while getTotalShares()>0 (sweep/attribute residual to a protocol sink), or document the sequencing hazard so the integrator does not relinquish-to-zero with live residual shares.

findings.title: Integration assumption for deferred stable-staker M-05 wiring: caller MUST pay-out/write-off principal to its end user BEFORE calling relinquishPrincipal and MUST NOT re-credit the resulting reflax surplus to the same owner (else cross-protocol double-count)
findings.function: relinquishPrincipal (primitive staged ahead of its caller — no stable-staker callsite exists yet)
findings.rootCause: relinquishPrincipal is a primitive staged ahead of its consumer. There is currently NO callsite in stable-staker. The reflax-side write-down releases the backing vault value as surplus to remaining clients; if the future stable-staker caller both (a) fails to pay-out/write-off the principal to its end user before relinquishing AND (b) re-credits the resulting reflax surplus to the same owner, value is double-counted across protocols (would be a cross-protocol Medium).
findings.impact: If filed as H/M now it would be 'speculation on future code' (explicitly known-invalid per CLAUDE.md). Recorded instead as a spec-conformance / integration assumption note bound to the deferred stable-staker M-05 implementation, so the wiring is audited against this constraint when it lands.
sources: Tier-2/Tier-3 prose finding #2 (stable-staker M-05 integration assumption)
findings.crossReference: stable-staker M-05 (fingerprint 0dca43f3, valid Medium, owner-accepted, pro-rata-haircut fix DEFERRED pending exactly this reflax relinquishPrincipal story — per MEMORY stable-staker-m05-fix-pending-vault notes).
findings.ledgerCollision: none — distinct from F-01/F-02 spec-conformance entries (different subject); this is the cross-protocol integration assumption channel.
findings.recommendation: Record in spec-conformance.md. When stable-staker wires relinquishPrincipal: assert the caller pays-out/writes-off principal to the end user before relinquishing, and does NOT re-credit the reflax surplus to the same owner. Re-evaluate at Medium severity at that integration point, not now.
